blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The conversations that shape a company's trajectory are rarely the ones recorded in the minutes. They are the one-to-ones between two senior people, on difficult topics that neither fully wants to raise, where the right and the wrong sentence are only a few words apart — and the consequences of each are quite different.

A skilled senior operator prepares differently for these. They do not rehearse a script; they rehearse a stance. What is the minimum they need the other person to walk away with? What is the maximum they are willing to publicly commit to? What are the three sentences they must not say, regardless of how provocative the conversation becomes? That quiet pre-work, done alone, is what allows them to stay composed when it matters.

The language itself is a craft. Diplomatic register is not evasion; it is precision. "That would be a difficult conversation to have with the board" is both a warning and an invitation, depending on tone. "I wonder whether that is entirely consistent with what we agreed in March" forces a specific question without shutting down the relationship. These are learned, not natural, and they are what distinguishes senior communication from merely loud communication.

items.q: According to the text, where do the conversations that shape a company's trajectory usually happen?
options: In the recorded minutes of board meetings
In one-to-ones between two senior people
items.why: "They are the one-to-ones between two senior people" — não o que fica nas atas.

items.q: What does the skilled operator rehearse before a hard conversation?
items.why: "They do not rehearse a script; they rehearse a stance."

items.q: The author claims diplomatic register is…
options: a polite way of evading the issue
a sign of weakness under pressure
items.why: "Diplomatic register is not evasion; it is precision."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Preparation done alone shapes how you perform in the room.
The most consequential conversations are often unrecorded.
Speaking bluntly and loudly is the mark of a strong senior leader.
The same sentence can act as both a warning and an invitation.
items.why: Inferência: o texto contrasta "senior communication" com "merely loud communication" — volume não é força.

items.q: The line "I wonder whether that is entirely consistent with what we agreed in March" suggests that the author values…
options: raising a pointed question while protecting the relationship
items.why: Inferência: "forces a specific question without shutting down the relationship" — precisão sem romper o vínculo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James numa conversa individual com um colega sênior. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for making the time. I wanted to keep this between the two of us, off the record, before it hardens into something either of us has to defend in front of the board.

I think we both know the disagreement over the pricing model has started to cost us. My people are hearing one thing from your team and something quite different from mine, and they are beginning to choose sides. That is the part that worries me — not the strategy itself, but what the friction is doing underneath it.

I am not asking you to concede the point today. I would simply ask whether the current position is entirely consistent with what the three of us agreed back in March. Because if it isn't, that is a difficult conversation to have upstairs, and I would much rather have it here, quietly, with you.

What I am proposing is this: we hold the public line for a fortnight, we take the numbers apart together, just us, and we walk into the next meeting with one voice — whichever way it lands. I would rather lose the argument to you in private than win it in a room where everyone is watching.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does James want to keep the conversation off the record?
options: Because the topic is confidential to shareholders
So there is no evidence if it goes wrong
Before it hardens into something they must defend to the board
So he can deny it happened later
items.why: "before it hardens into something either of us has to defend in front of the board."

items.q: What does James say worries him most?
options: What the friction is doing to the teams underneath
items.why: "not the strategy itself, but what the friction is doing underneath it."

items.q: How does James raise the March agreement?
options: He asks the board to arbitrate it
He accuses his peer of breaking it
He asks whether the current position is entirely consistent with it
items.why: "whether the current position is entirely consistent with what the three of us agreed back in March" — forçar a pergunta sem acusar.

items.q: What does James most likely mean by "a difficult conversation to have upstairs"?
options: A private chat with his own team
A meeting in a different office
A discussion escalated to senior leadership or the board
items.why: Inferência: "upstairs" é eufemismo para a instância superior — um aviso implícito de escalonamento.

items.q: "I would rather lose the argument to you in private than win it in a room where everyone is watching." This suggests James…
options: cares more about the relationship and unity than about being right
wants to avoid the meeting altogether
is certain he will lose the argument
is trying to intimidate his peer
items.why: Inferência: ele prioriza sair com "one voice" acima de vencer publicamente.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "He asked for a one-to-one before the board met." A one-to-one is…
options: a private conversation between two people
items.why: One-to-one = conversa individual, entre duas pessoas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "She didn't rehearse a script; she rehearsed a ___ — what she stood for, regardless of how the talk went."
items.why: Stance = postura: a posição que se defende, não um roteiro fixo.

items.q: "'That would be awkward for the board' was an implicit warning." An implicit warning is…
options: a threat stated openly and directly
a caution conveyed without being spelled out
items.why: Implicit warning = aviso implícito: alerta que não é dito com todas as letras.

items.q: "She kept her composure under pressure even as the questions turned hostile." This means she…
options: stayed calm and controlled when it was hard
raised her voice to match theirs
items.why: Composure under pressure = serenidade sob pressão, manter-se calmo no momento difícil.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "He said it was ___, so nothing would ever appear in an email."
items.why: Off the record = extraoficial: sem registro, nada por escrito.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sensíveis entre pares seniores. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's hold the line for a fortnight before we say anything publicly." To hold the line means to…
options: put the matter to a vote
maintain the agreed position without changing it
items.why: Hold the line = manter a posição firme, sem recuar por ora.

items.q: "He wouldn't back down, even when the room turned against him." To back down means to…
options: withdraw from a position under pressure
items.why: Back down = ceder, recuar de uma posição diante de pressão.

items.q: "I didn't want to put you on the spot in front of the board." To put someone on the spot means to…
options: force them to respond or decide in an uncomfortable moment
items.why: Put someone on the spot = colocar alguém em saia justa, forçando resposta na hora.

items.q: "Before I escalate, let's talk it through quietly, just the two of us." To talk something through means to…
options: report it to a third party
discuss it thoroughly until it's resolved
mention it briefly and move on
items.why: Talk something through = discutir a fundo até esclarecer.

items.q: "If we can't agree here, I'll have to take it upstairs." To take something upstairs means to…
options: escalate it to more senior leadership
items.why: Take it upstairs = levar à instância superior, escalar — o aviso implícito de James.
